other open-source Python optimization packages out there. It can
thus be understood as an attempt to provide the best of all worlds
when it comes to solving optimization problems with Python. All
the credit for implementing the invoked optimizers goes to the
original package providers.

name: iwopy
raw_meta_yaml:
{% set name = "iwopy" %}
{% set version = "0.5.0" %}

package:
  name: {{ name|lower }}
  version: {{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/FraunhoferIWES/iwopy/archive/v{{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: f2e68f909ce1ca982d8287a75e8b61f926c421b64d635d18a344ea2272d37ecc

build:
  noarch: python
  script: {{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
  number: 0

requirements:
  host:
    - python {{ python_min }}
    - pip
    - setuptools >=84.0.0
    - wheel
  run:
    - python >={{ python_min }}
    - matplotlib-base >=3.8
    - numpy >=1.26
    - scipy >=1.12

test:
  imports:
    - iwopy
  requires:
    - python {{ python_min }}
    - pip
    - pytest >=9.0.3
    - pymoo >=0.6
    - pygmo >=2.19
  source_files:
    - tests
    - examples/callbacks
  commands:
    - pip check
    - pytest tests

about:
  home: https://github.com/FraunhoferIWES/iwopy
  summary: Fraunhofer IWES optimization tools in Python
  description: |
    The iwopy package is a meta package that provides interfaces to
    other open-source Python optimization packages out there. It can
    thus be understood as an attempt to provide the best of all worlds
    when it comes to solving optimization problems with Python. All
    the credit for implementing the invoked optimizers goes to the
    original package providers.
  license: MIT
  license_file: LICENSE

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - SchmJo
